common.ops_best_practices: Best practices: anticipate peaks (seasonality, public holidays), use proper export packaging (blocking, strapping), secure ad valorem insurance and keep a buffer on critical deadlines.
common.incoterms_intro: Incoterms shift control, cost allocation and risk transfer along the chain. Typical patterns: FOB/CIF for standard sea flows; DAP/DDP for door-to-door experience.
incoterms_list: FOB: buyer controls main carriage; requires logistics maturity
CFR: seller pays main carriage; risk transfers at loading
CIF: seller pays freight + insurance; risk transfers at loading
DAP/DDP: extended coverage by seller; import clearance and taxes depending on variant
common.delivered_cost_note: Always compare FCL vs LCL on total delivered cost, not only on the rate per m³.
checklist: Commercial invoice, packing list, BL (to be validated)
Certificate of origin and specific documents (if required)
Ad valorem insurance and packaging photos
Consignee details, delivery time window, site constraints
common.cbm_note: Indicative only: 20' ≈ 33 m³, 40' ≈ 67 m³. Tolerances and weight/volume limits depend on carrier and service.

france_china.label: France ↔ China

faq.q: FCL or LCL: what to choose on the France–China corridor?
faq.a: Above roughly 13–15 m³, FCL is often more economical and more secure (fewer handlings). Below that, LCL remains relevant to optimise budget.
FOB/CIF are common on China flows; DAP/DDP offer extended coverage. The choice depends on desired control and risk profile.
Yes: BL, commercial invoice, packing list, any required certificates; plus compliance checks and customs assistance.

faq.q: Can rail freight replace sea freight?
faq.a: On some corridors, rail offers around 18–22 days transit. It is a good compromise between air and sea in terms of speed and cost.

faq.q: Which periods are the most constrained?
faq.a: Chinese New Year and Q4 before Christmas. It's better to book early and keep alternative services available.
